doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Billy Taylor years and the greats
title: Lush Life session at Van Gelder's and self-criticism
summary: Details of the session: separated from drummer Arthur Taylor, Red Garland absent, trio only; May regrets his beat.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: He’d ask me, “You know this tune?” And he said, “Well we’re going to do like, I want you to play this kind of an intro” [scats]. He would just tell me what he wanted and I would do my best. But I was so scared. I was so scared. That date, the takes that came out, not very favorable in my direction because Arthur Taylor was way — like almost in the other room. We did it at Rudy VanGelder’s, in his living room at that time you know. And he really separated us. So I didn’t really lock up with the drummer like I really wanted to. And Red Garland called halfway through the date and said that his car broke down so he wouldn’t make the date, so we wound up doing the whole thing as a trio, which was another frightening thing for me.
But I’ve heard some other takes from that same session where I played much better than the one that came out. As a matter of fact I have a copy at home.

But I shudder when people tell me — we talk about that date — because it wasn’t a very, completely happy experience for me, because of what I failed to do as far as the beat was concerned. You can go back to that again.
Wow. Do you suppose you are your own worst critic?
Oh I know that. I know that. I know I am.
